proof: Nats-Msg-Id is the SHA-256 of the canonical immutable event JSON, including tenant_id and event_id, so exact retries deduplicate while conflicting tenant or payload retries reach canonical conflict handling.
Runtime summaries persist independently by the composite tenant_id and runtime_id identity.
An empty batch or a batch with zero durable receipts returns HTTP 400; a mixed batch returns HTTP 202 only when at least one receipt is durable and reports partially_accepted with both counts.
Missing bearer authority, forbidden tenant scope, payload and header mismatch, cross-tenant readback, unscoped legacy lineage, and unauthorized DLQ replay fail closed.
HTTP success follows the JetStream persistence PubAck, and the canonical writer acknowledges the broker receipt only after Postgres succeeds or a failed event is fsynced to the replayable DLQ.
Lifecycle identity retains tenant_id, trace_id, aggregate identity, sequence, and correlation envelope while heartbeats update freshness fields.

Against NATS JetStream 2.11 file storage, a child process fetched the accepted event and exited with code 23 before acknowledgement; a replacement durable consumer recovered the exact event and acknowledged it once.
After persisted runtime-summary store reload, all nine current tenant and runtime identities retained lifecycle correlation; cross-tenant and ambiguous unscoped reads remained isolated.
Canonical write failure produces an fsynced tenant-scoped DLQ record before broker acknowledgement, preserving an operator-authorized replay path.
This telemetry slice grants no broker, allocation, deployment, runtime-control, or live-capital mutation authority.
